published flight list — and scored identically. No value in @sec-defaults
became a default without passing this stage.

Two differences between the two stages remain, and both are named here rather
than left to be discovered in the residual:

1. the pipeline filters zones by radius **band** — the H3 ring the zone was
   generated at — while the sweep cuts on exact distance;
2. the sweep smooths barometric altitude across the flight-level boundary and
   the pipeline applies the cut first, so its smoothing window is truncated
   there.

A third difference, and by far the largest, has been **closed**: the pipeline
used to keep only the candidates at the minimum H3 ring count and measure exact
distance only among the survivors, so an aerodrome one ring further out was
eliminated before its distance was ever computed. It now carries every
candidate in the joined disk through to an exact-distance ranking, which is
what the sweep always did. That change is the subject of the rest of this
section.

```{r pipeline-fidelity}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(modes) && !is.null(trend) && !is.null(grid)) {
  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(modes)), function(i) {
    r <- modes[i, ]
    do.call(rbind, lapply(c("adep", "ades"), function(role) data.frame(
      Run = r$run, Role = toupper(role),
      Mode = r[[paste0(role, "_mode")]],
      Coverage = pct(r[[paste0(role, "_coverage")]]),
      Accuracy = pct(r[[paste0(role, "_accuracy")]]),
      Correct  = num(r[[paste0(role, "_correct")]]),
      Wrong    = num(r[[paste0(role, "_wrong")]]),
      Score    = num(r[[paste0(role, "_score")]]),
      check.names = FALSE)))
  }))
  print(kable(rows, row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))

  # The harness's own figure for the same setting, so the residual is visible
  # rather than implied.
  cat("\n**Harness against pipeline, at the same parameters:**\n\n")
  cmp <- do.call(rbind, list(
    local({
      h <- best_row(grid, "adep"); p <- modes[modes$run == "endpoint", ]
      data.frame(Role = "ADEP", Method = "endpoint",
                 `Harness score` = num(h$score),
                 `Pipeline score` = num(p$adep_score),
                 Residual = sgn(p$adep_score - h$score),
                 `Relative` = sprintf("%+.2f%%", 100 * (p$adep_score - h$score) / h$score),
                 check.names = FALSE)
    }),
    local({
      # From the `combined` run, not the `trend` run. A DetectionConfig holds
      # one trend setting, so the single-mode `trend` run has both roles at the
      # *departure* optimum and its arrival figure describes a setting nobody
      # recommends. `combined` is where trend runs at the arrival optimum.
      h <- best_row(trend[trend$stage == 1, ], "ades"); p <- modes[modes$run == "combined", ]
      data.frame(Role = "ADES", Method = "trend",
                 `Harness score` = num(h$score),
                 `Pipeline score` = num(p$ades_score),
                 Residual = sgn(p$ades_score - h$score),
                 `Relative` = sprintf("%+.2f%%", 100 * (p$ades_score - h$score) / h$score),
                 check.names = FALSE)
    })))
  print(kable(cmp, row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))
  cat("\nThe two rows could hardly be more different, and the difference is the single most important result on this page.\n")
  cat("\n`endpoint` **reproduces exactly**. That is not luck: the endpoint sweep filters the same cached candidate table the pipeline reads, applying the same rule, so harness and pipeline are the same computation and agree to the flight.\n")
  cat("\n`trend` **does not**, and the reason is the ranking rule. Both stages now rank candidate aerodromes on exact great-circle distance: the full set of aerodromes whose detection zone the aircraft passed through is carried forward, each candidate's own closest approach is computed, and the scheduled-service penalty is applied to that distance. Nothing is eliminated before it is measured.\n")
  cat("\nUntil this study that was true of the sweep only. The pipeline kept just the candidates at the minimum H3 *ring count* — an integer stepping about 5.2 km at resolution 7 — and applied the tie-break, and the penalty, within that surviving set alone. An aerodrome one ring further out was gone before the penalty could promote it, so a penalty tuned against exact distance did something weaker in production. The residual above is what remains once that rule is the same on both sides: the radius band and the truncated smoothing window, and nothing else.\n")
}
```

### The trend tuning re-walked inside the pipeline

The path below runs through `process_dai` itself. Each row **adds one parameter
change to the row above it** and rebuilds the whole flight list with everything
adopted so far, so row *n* differs from row *n−1* in exactly one value. It
answers which of the changes is doing the work, not which configuration to
ship — for that see @sec-verdict.

Both roles are produced by `trend` in every row, at the arrival tuning, because
that is the parameter set being walked. The departure columns are therefore a
diagnostic and not a recommendation: what ships takes departures from
`endpoint`.

It was run twice — once with the pipeline's original **H3 ring-count**
selection, and once with **exact-distance** ranking. The two disagree in sign,
which is the whole finding.

```{r pipeline-path}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
ppath <- cache("pipeline_path_v6.csv")
if (!is.null(ppath)) {
  # Rungs 0-4 walk the SEA-LEVEL tuning, so they are the same ladder version 6
  # published and are directly comparable to it. Rung 5 moves the datum and
  # nothing else, at the ceiling that admits the identical band -- which is
  # what makes its delta attributable to the datum rather than to a ceiling
  # that moved along with it.
  lab <- c(path0_legacy = "legacy constants",
           path1_penalty = "+ scheduled-service penalty",
           path2_ceiling = "+ altitude ceiling",
           path3_margin = "+ vote margin",
           path4_radius = "+ radius",
           path5_datum = "+ field-elevation datum")
  ppath <- ppath[order(match(ppath$run, names(lab))), ]
  sc <- ppath$ades_score

  # The ring-ranked run, read from its own CSV rather than typed in. An earlier
  # draft of this chunk carried these five numbers as R literals -- on a page
  # whose whole argument is that hand-copied figures cannot be trusted.
  rp <- cache("pipeline_path_ring_v6.csv")
  rp <- rp[order(match(rp$run, names(lab))), ]
  ring <- rp$ades_score

  print(kable(data.frame(
    Step = lab[ppath$run],
    `Ring: score` = num(ring),
    `Ring: gain` = c("—", sgn(diff(ring))),
    `Exact: score` = num(sc),
    `Exact: gain` = c("—", sgn(diff(sc))),
    Coverage = pct(ppath$ades_coverage), Accuracy = pct(ppath$ades_accuracy),
    check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))

  cat(sprintf("\nUnder ring selection the tuning is worth %s; under exact distance it is worth %s. The altitude ceiling is the step that flips hardest — %s against %s — and it is the step that admits samples from higher up, where more aerodromes share a ring and the ring rule is least able to separate them.\n",
              sgn(ring[length(ring)] - ring[1]), sgn(sc[length(sc)] - sc[1]),
              sgn(diff(ring)[2]), sgn(diff(sc)[2])))

  # The fifth rung, reported separately: it is the only step that moves the
  # datum, so it is the only one whose delta is the datum's own contribution
  # inside the pipeline.
  if ("path5_datum" %in% ppath$run && length(sc) >= 6) {
    cat(sprintf("\nThe fifth rung is the datum, and it is the reason this version exists. Moving `trend`'s altitude cut from a flight level onto the aerodrome's own field elevation — at the ceiling admitting the identical band, so nothing else moves with it — is worth %s under exact distance and %s under ring selection. @sec-datum takes that apart by field elevation, which is where the number stops being a single figure and starts being an explanation.\n",
                sgn(diff(sc)[5]), sgn(diff(ring)[5])))
  }
  cat("\nSo the sweep harness was never over-estimating. It was measuring a *better algorithm* — one that measures every candidate before choosing — and the pipeline has now adopted it. `trend_rank_by` defaults to `\"haversine\"`; `DetectionConfig.legacy()` still returns `\"ring\"`, so every published flight list stays reproducible.\n")
}
```

### The pipeline's own optimum

The path adopts the values the *sweep* preferred. Whether those are also the
**pipeline's** optima is a separate question, and it is answered by sweeping
the altitude ceiling and radius through `process_dai` directly — on the datum
that ships, so the ceilings below are feet above field elevation.

Both roles are produced by `trend` in every cell of this grid. Held fixed
throughout: vote margin 2, scheduled-service penalty 10 NM, ranking on exact
distance. The vote margin is a `trend` parameter only — the majority one
direction must win by across the smoothed altitude samples before a track is
called a departure or an arrival. `endpoint` has no votes; it reads one fix.

The grid runs from 3,000 ft to 10,000 ft above field, which is far enough to
find the arrival optimum and **not** far enough to close the departure side —
see @sec-limitations. It carries both 6,000 ft and 6,100 ft deliberately: the
first is what ships and the second is what the research sweep preferred, and
the sweep grid never contained the shipped value, so the two had never been
compared until this table.

```{r pipeline-trend-grid}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
tg <- cache("trend_grid_v6.csv")
if (!is.null(tg)) {
  # `trend_ceiling` means the right thing on either datum: feet above field
  # when the datum is `field`, a flight level when it is `msl`. Keying on
  # `trend_max_fl` would collapse every row of a height grid onto one cap,
  # because that field is inert while the field datum is in force.
  CEIL <- if ("trend_ceiling" %in% names(tg)) "trend_ceiling" else "trend_max_fl"
  dtm <- if ("trend_max_datum" %in% names(tg)) unique(tg$trend_max_datum)[1] else "msl"
  tg <- tg[order(tg[[CEIL]], tg$trend_radius_nm), ]
  wide <- function(col) {
    w <- reshape(tg[, c(CEIL, "trend_radius_nm", col)],
                 idvar = CEIL, timevar = "trend_radius_nm",
                 direction = "wide")
    w <- w[order(w[[CEIL]]), ]
    names(w) <- sub(paste0("^", col, "\\."), "", names(w))
    w
  }
  a <- wide("ades_score"); d <- wide("adep_score")
  tab <- data.frame(Ceiling = vapply(a[[CEIL]], cap_label, "", datum = dtm),
                    `ADES 20 NM` = num(a[["20"]]), `ADES 30 NM` = num(a[["30"]]),
                    `ADEP 20 NM` = num(d[["20"]]), `ADEP 30 NM` = num(d[["30"]]),
                    check.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("\n**Score by altitude ceiling (rows) and radius in NM (columns), through the pipeline, at vote margin 2 and penalty 10 NM.** Ceilings are %s. Departures are shown for completeness -- they are served by `endpoint`, so that half is a check rather than a recommendation.\n\n",
              if (identical(dtm, "field")) "heights above field elevation" else "flight levels"))
  print(kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))

  b <- tg[which.max(tg$ades_score), ]
  bd <- tg[which.max(tg$adep_score), ]
  cat(sprintf("\nArrivals peak at **%s / %g NM**. Departures climb to **%s**, but departures are served by `endpoint`, so that column is a check rather than a recommendation.\n",
              cap_label(b[[CEIL]], dtm), b$trend_radius_nm,
              cap_label(bd[[CEIL]], dtm)))

  # Whether the arrival optimum is interior is a property of this grid, not a
  # standing fact -- it was one in version 6 and the grid has since changed.
  # Asserting it in prose would be asserting the previous grid's shape.
  caps <- sort(unique(tg[[CEIL]]))
  if (length(caps) > 2) {
    interior <- b[[CEIL]] > min(caps) && b[[CEIL]] < max(caps)
    cat(sprintf("\nThat arrival peak is %s of the grid, so it %s.\n",
                if (interior) "interior, with the score falling away on both sides"
                else "at an edge",
                if (interior) "is an optimum rather than the best cell that happened to be tried"
                else "may not be an optimum: the grid should be widened before the value is trusted"))
  }
  # Which radius each role prefers, read off the grid rather than asserted.
  # Version 6 stated that both roles prefer the tighter radius at every cell,
  # and cited that as the stronger evidence for adopting 20 NM. On this datum
  # it is not true for arrivals, so it is computed here instead of repeated.
  radii <- sort(unique(tg$trend_radius_nm))
  if (length(radii) == 2) {
    tight <- radii[1]; wide <- radii[2]
    pref <- function(role) {
      caps <- sort(unique(tg[[CEIL]]))
      vapply(caps, function(c) {
        a <- tg[[paste0(role, "_score")]][tg[[CEIL]] == c & tg$trend_radius_nm == tight]
        b <- tg[[paste0(role, "_score")]][tg[[CEIL]] == c & tg$trend_radius_nm == wide]
        if (!length(a) || !length(b)) NA_real_ else a[1] - b[1]
      }, numeric(1))
    }
    da <- pref("ades"); dd <- pref("adep")
    caps <- sort(unique(tg[[CEIL]]))
    cat(sprintf("\n**Which radius wins depends on the ceiling, and on the role.** Departures prefer the tighter %g NM at %d of %d ceilings; arrivals prefer it at only %d, and at every ceiling from %s upward they prefer the wider %g NM — which includes the ceiling that ships.\n",
                tight, sum(dd > 0, na.rm = TRUE), length(caps),
                sum(da > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
                cap_label(min(caps[which(da < 0)]), dtm), wide))
    cat(sprintf("\nThat matters because version 6 reported the opposite — that both roles prefer the tighter radius at every cell — and cited it as the stronger evidence for lowering `trend_radius_nm` to %g NM. On the datum that ships, the grid does not support that for arrivals, which are the role `trend` actually serves. The value was never applied to `DetectionConfig` regardless, and this study does not renew the recommendation.\n",
                tight))
  }

  cat("\nOne caveat, stated rather than buried: the grid holds the **vote margin** fixed at 2 while varying the ceiling and radius. That value therefore rests on the sweep harness alone, and is the weakest-supported of the shipped parameters.\n")
}
```

## Why each value, and not its neighbour {#sec-justification}

A recommendation is only as good as the evidence that picked it, so every value
the sweeps select appears below with the score at that value, the score at the
adjacent grid points, and the score at the legacy value. The last
column is the one that matters most for trusting the number: a value on a broad
**plateau** is a safe recommendation even from a single sample, because its
neighbours score nearly the same and a little noise cannot move it far. A value
on a sharp isolated **peak** may be partly the sample's noise, and is flagged
as such however good its score.

::: {.callout-important}
## These are the sweeps' choices, not the shipped ones
The `Chosen` column below is the **harness argmax**, which is what this section
exists to scrutinise. For `trend`, @sec-pipeline is what settles whether each
value survives in the pipeline — and under exact-distance ranking they do, which
is why the harness numbers below and the shipped values in @sec-defaults now
agree. They are still kept apart, because for a period they did *not* agree,
and a sweep preference is only ever evidence until the pipeline confirms it.
:::

```{r justification}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

# The score at one grid point, holding every other swept parameter at the
# chosen value. This is what makes the neighbour columns meaningful: they vary
# one parameter at a time rather than reporting the best cell that happens to
# contain that value.
at <- function(d, role, fixed, param, value, k = K_DEFAULT) {
  sel <- rep(TRUE, nrow(d))
  for (nm in names(fixed)) if (nm != param) sel <- sel & d[[nm]] == fixed[[nm]]
  sel <- sel & d[[param]] == value
  x <- with_metrics(d[sel, , drop = FALSE], role, k)
  if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  x$score[1]
}

# One row of the table: chosen value, its two neighbours on the grid, and the
# shape that follows from them.
just_row <- function(d, role, chosen, param, label, orig_value, k = K_DEFAULT,
                     fixed_names) {
  fixed <- as.list(chosen[fixed_names])
  vals  <- sort(unique(d[[param]]))
  i     <- match(chosen[[param]], vals)
  s_ch  <- at(d, role, fixed, param, vals[i], k)
  s_lo  <- if (i > 1) at(d, role, fixed, param, vals[i - 1], k) else NA_real_
  s_hi  <- if (i < length(vals)) at(d, role, fixed, param, vals[i + 1], k) else NA_real_
  s_or  <- at(d, role, fixed, param, orig_value, k)

  # Plateau if the better neighbour is within 0.5% of the chosen score --
  # a margin far smaller than any effect the report argues from.
  nb   <- c(s_lo, s_hi); nb <- nb[!is.na(nb)]
  gap  <- if (length(nb)) (s_ch - max(nb)) / s_ch else NA_real_
  shape <- if (is.na(gap)) "—" else if (gap < 0.005) "plateau" else "peak"

  data.frame(
    Role = toupper(role), Parameter = label,
    Legacy = orig_value, `Sweep argmax` = chosen[[param]],
    `Score at legacy` = ifelse(is.na(s_or), "—", num(s_or)),
    `Score at argmax`     = num(s_ch),
    `Neighbour below`   = ifelse(is.na(s_lo), "—", num(s_lo)),
    `Neighbour above`   = ifelse(is.na(s_hi), "—", num(s_hi)),
    `Δ vs legacy`   = ifelse(is.na(s_or), "—", sgn(s_ch - s_or)),
    Shape = shape, check.names = FALSE)
}

if (!is.null(trend) && !is.null(grid)) {
  s1 <- trend[trend$stage == 1, ]
  tf <- c("fl_cap", "margin", "radius_nm")
  ef <- c("radius_nm", "height_ft")

  rows <- list()
  # trend, for the role it is recommended for (arrivals), against the
  # production constants: FL40, margin 4, 30 NM.
  bt <- best_row(s1, "ades")
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- just_row(s1, "ades", bt, "fl_cap",    "trend ceiling",
                                     if (identical(datum_of(trend), "msl")) 40 else 4100,
                                     fixed_names = tf)
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- just_row(s1, "ades", bt, "margin",    "trend vote margin",   4, fixed_names = tf)
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- just_row(s1, "ades", bt, "radius_nm", "trend radius (NM)",  30, fixed_names = tf)

  # endpoint, for departures, against the version 4.5 operating point that the
  # pipeline currently defaults to: 40 NM, 15,000 ft.
  be <- best_row(grid, "adep")
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- just_row(grid, "adep", be, "radius_nm", "endpoint radius (NM)",    40, fixed_names = ef)
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- just_row(grid, "adep", be, "height_ft", "endpoint height (ft)", 15000, fixed_names = ef)

  print(kable(do.call(rbind, rows), row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))
  cat("\nThe penalty is treated separately because it is not a geometric parameter: it re-ranks candidates without changing how many are answered, so its sweep holds the geometry fixed and appears in @sec-penalty.\n")
}
```

### Which change is actually doing the work

The table above varies one parameter at a time around the chosen setting, which
shows whether each value is defensible but not how much each contributes to the
total gain. This walks the whole distance instead: from the legacy constants to
the recommended setting, changing one parameter per step.

**How to read it.** Each row *adds* its change to everything in the rows above
and keeps it — row 5 has all four changes applied, not just the radius. `Gain`
is that row's score minus the previous row's, so it is the marginal worth of
that one change given everything already adopted. All rows are arrivals under
`trend`, in the research sweep.

```{r trend-path}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(trend)) {
  s1 <- trend[trend$stage == 1, ]
  b  <- best_row(s1, "ades")
  s0 <- with_metrics(trend[trend$stage == 0, ], "ades")

  # Each step adopts one recommended value and holds the rest at production's.
  # The order is deliberate: the penalty first, because it is the parameter
  # production does not apply at all, and the geometry after.
  cellv <- function(fl, mg, rd, pn) {
    x <- with_metrics(trend[trend$fl_cap == fl & trend$margin == mg &
                            trend$radius_nm == rd & trend$penalty_nm == pn, ],
                      "ades")
    if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0) NA else x$score[1]
  }
  # The legacy ceiling, on whichever datum this sweep was measured.
  #
  # `legacy()` is FL40. On the above-field grid the comparable ceiling is its
  # height equivalent, 4,100 ft — and since the grid does not contain 4,100
  # either, the nearest point stands in. Hardcoding 40 here would make every
  # `cellv` call return NA on a field-datum sweep, and the `ok` filter below
  # would then drop the affected rows *silently*: a shorter ladder that still
  # renders, still sums to 100%, and is missing its first two steps.
  dtm <- datum_of(trend)
  caps <- sort(unique(s1$fl_cap))
  lc <- if (identical(dtm, "msl")) 40 else caps[which.min(abs(caps - 4100))]
  steps <- list(
    list(lab = sprintf("legacy constants (%s, margin 4, 30 NM, no penalty)",
                       cap_label(lc, dtm)),
         s = s0$score),
    list(lab = sprintf("+ scheduled-service penalty of %g NM", b$penalty_nm),
         s = cellv(lc, 4, 30, b$penalty_nm)),
    list(lab = sprintf("+ altitude ceiling %s", cap_label(b$fl_cap, dtm)),
         s = cellv(b$fl_cap, 4, 30, b$penalty_nm)),
    list(lab = sprintf("+ vote margin %g", b$margin),
         s = cellv(b$fl_cap, b$margin, 30, b$penalty_nm)),
    list(lab = sprintf("+ radius %g NM", b$radius_nm),
         s = cellv(b$fl_cap, b$margin, b$radius_nm, b$penalty_nm)))

  ok <- !sapply(steps, function(x) is.na(x$s))
  if (any(!ok)) {
    # Loud, because a dropped rung leaves a ladder that still renders, still
    # sums to 100%, and quietly attributes the missing step's gain to its
    # neighbour.
    cat(sprintf("\n::: {.callout-warning}\n## %d rung(s) of this ladder are missing\n\nThe sweep grid has no cell for: %s. The percentages below are shares of the gain across the rungs that *are* present, not of the whole distance from legacy to recommended.\n:::\n\n",
                sum(!ok),
                paste(sub("^\\+ ", "", sapply(steps[!ok], function(x) x$lab)),
                      collapse = "; ")))
  }
  steps <- steps[ok]
  sc <- sapply(steps, function(x) x$s)
  tab <- data.frame(
    Step = sapply(steps, function(x) x$lab),
    Score = num(sc),
    `Gain from this step` = c("—", sgn(diff(sc))),
    `Share of total gain` = c("—", sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * diff(sc) / (sc[length(sc)] - sc[1]))),
    check.names = FALSE)
  print(kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))

  dom <- which.max(diff(sc))
  cat(sprintf("\nThe gain is not spread evenly. **%s** accounts for %.0f%% of it on its own. That is worth stating plainly: the single most valuable change to arrival detection is not a tuned threshold at all, but applying to `trend` the scheduled-service tie-break that `endpoint` already had and `trend` never did.\n",
              sub("^\\+ ", "", steps[[dom + 1]]$lab),
              100 * max(diff(sc)) / (sc[length(sc)] - sc[1])))
  cat(sprintf("\nBy contrast the radius step is worth %s flights out of %s here — inside what one three-day sample can resolve, and on this evidence alone it would not justify moving a published constant. Version 6 adopted it anyway, citing the pipeline grid as stronger evidence. On the datum that ships, that grid no longer supports it: see @sec-pipeline, where arrivals prefer the *wider* 30 NM at every ceiling from 6,000 ft up, which is where the shipped ceiling sits. The 20 NM recommendation was never applied to `DetectionConfig` in any case, and this study does not renew it.\n",
              num(sc[length(sc)] - sc[length(sc) - 1]), num(sc[length(sc)])))
}
```

## The verdict {#sec-verdict}

```{r verdict}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(modes)) {
  m <- function(run, field) {
    v <- modes[[field]][modes$run == run]
    if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else v[1]
  }
  tot <- function(run) m(run, "adep_score") + m(run, "ades_score")
  runs <- modes$run[order(-(modes$adep_score + modes$ades_score))]

  # `recommended` and `combined` are the same configuration built two ways --
  # from DetectionConfig() and by naming the fields -- and they agree field for
  # field. Labelling both makes that visible instead of looking like two
  # different recommendations.
  label <- c(legacy = "legacy — the algorithm published before 2026",
             trend = "trend, departure parameters both roles",
             endpoint = "endpoint, both roles",
             nearest = "nearest (traffic library)",
             combined = "**SHIPPED** endpoint + exact-distance trend",
             recommended = "the same, built from `DetectionConfig()`")
  print(kable(data.frame(
    Configuration = ifelse(is.na(label[modes$run]), modes$run, label[modes$run]),
    ADEP = paste0(modes$adep_mode, ""), ADES = paste0(modes$ades_mode, ""),
    `ADEP coverage` = pct(modes$adep_coverage),
    `ADEP accuracy` = pct(modes$adep_accuracy),
    `ADEP score` = num(modes$adep_score),
    `ADES coverage` = pct(modes$ades_coverage),
    `ADES accuracy` = pct(modes$ades_accuracy),
    `ADES score` = num(modes$ades_score),
    Total = num(modes$adep_score + modes$ades_score),
    check.names = FALSE)[order(-(modes$adep_score + modes$ades_score)), ],
    row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))

  cat("\nEach row is a complete configuration — which method names departures, which names arrivals — not a step in a sequence. The rows are alternatives to choose between.\n")
  cat(sprintf("\nThe recommended configuration is the **%s** row: `endpoint` for departures, exact-distance `trend` for arrivals. It scores **%s against legacy's %s, a gain of %s** on a three-day sample of %s flights, and every figure in that table is a real pipeline run scored against Network Manager ground truth.\n",
              SHIPPED, num(tot(SHIPPED)), num(tot("legacy")),
              sgn(tot(SHIPPED) - tot("legacy")), num(N_GT)))
  cat("\nIt is the shipped configuration in the strict sense: its trend cap, radius, vote margin, penalty and ranking rule, and its endpoint radius, height and penalty, were checked field by field against `DetectionConfig()`. The row is what the pipeline produces, not an approximation of it.\n")
  cat(sprintf("\nThe `recommended` row is the same configuration constructed the other way — by instantiating `DetectionConfig()` rather than by naming each field — and it lands within %s of `%s` in total. Two independent constructions of the shipped settings agreeing to that margin is the check that the recommendation and the code have not drifted apart.\n",
              num(abs(tot("recommended") - tot(SHIPPED))), SHIPPED))
}
```

### What is being recommended, and why

```{r verdict-detail}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(modes) && !is.null(grid)) {
  m <- function(run, field) modes[[field]][modes$run == run][1]
  tg <- cache("trend_grid_v6.csv")
  cat(sprintf("**Departures — `endpoint`, %g NM radius, %s ft above field elevation, %g NM scheduled-service penalty.** That height is `endpoint_height_ft`, a height above the aerodrome's own elevation — not a flight level, and not related to the flight-level caps swept for `trend`, which departures do not use. Score %s against legacy's %s, a gain of %s. The clearest result in the study: an interior optimum in both parameters, better than `trend` at every exchange rate tried, and the pipeline reproduces the sweep exactly -- the endpoint sweep filters the same cached candidate table the pipeline reads, so the tuned figure *is* the pipeline figure.\n\n",
              best_row(grid, "adep")$radius_nm,
              format(best_row(grid, "adep")$height_ft, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE),
              best_row(grid, "adep")$penalty_nm,
              num(m(SHIPPED, "adep_score")), num(m("legacy", "adep_score")),
              sgn(m(SHIPPED, "adep_score") - m("legacy", "adep_score"))))

  if (!is.null(tg)) {
    b <- tg[which.max(tg$ades_score), ]
    cat(sprintf("**Arrivals — `trend` at %s, vote margin %g, %g NM, %g NM penalty, ranked on exact distance.** Measured as an algorithm, on a trend-only flight list, that is %s against legacy's %s -- a gain of %s, won by converting %s silences into correct answers for %s extra wrong ones.\n\n",
                # From the pipeline frame, not the sweep: it carries the datum
                # it actually ran on, so the label cannot disagree with the run.
                cap_label(if (!is.null(b$trend_ceiling)) b$trend_ceiling else b$trend_max_fl,
                          if (!is.null(b$trend_max_datum)) b$trend_max_datum else "msl"),
                b$trend_vote_margin, b$trend_radius_nm,
                b$trend_sched_penalty_nm,
                num(b$ades_score), num(m("legacy", "ades_score")),
                sgn(b$ades_score - m("legacy", "ades_score")),
                num(b$ades_correct - m("legacy", "ades_correct")),
                num(b$ades_wrong - m("legacy", "ades_wrong"))))

    cat(sprintf("Inside the combined flight list the arrival half reads %s, %s against legacy rather than the %s just quoted. The difference is not the algorithm. Taking departures from `endpoint` adds tracks `trend` never produced, and where two share an aircraft, callsign and date, the scoring alignment awards the flight to whichever starts closest to the actual off-block time -- sometimes now a departure-only track carrying no arrival. Accuracy *rises* in the merged table (%s against %s) while coverage falls, which is the signature of lost pairings rather than wrong names.\n\n",
                num(m(SHIPPED, "ades_score")),
                sgn(m(SHIPPED, "ades_score") - m("legacy", "ades_score")),
                sgn(b$ades_score - m("legacy", "ades_score")),
                pct(m(SHIPPED, "ades_accuracy")), pct(m("legacy", "ades_accuracy"))))
  }

  cat("**One weak link, stated plainly.** The vote margin of 2 comes from the sweep harness; the pipeline grid held it fixed while varying the cap and radius. Every other shipped value was measured through `process_dai`. If one parameter in this recommendation is going to fail on a fresh sample, that is the one.\n")
}
```

  cat(sprintf("`nearest` — the unconditional rule the `traffic` library uses — answers far more often than anything else here (%s of departures, %s of arrivals) and is right far less often (%s and %s). Scored, it is last by a wide margin: %s against the recommendation's %s.\n",
              pct(m("nearest", "adep_coverage")), pct(m("nearest", "ades_coverage")),
              pct(m("nearest", "adep_accuracy")), pct(m("nearest", "ades_accuracy")),

              num(m("recommended", "adep_score") + m("recommended", "ades_score"))))
  cat("\nThat is not a criticism of `traffic`, which is solving a different problem: it names the nearest aerodrome and leaves the judgement to the caller. It is, however, the measurement that justifies OPDI carrying its own rule rather than adopting that one.\n")

## By aerodrome class {#sec-per-type}

The candidate set is large and medium aerodromes only, so a flight whose true
aerodrome is a small airfield or a heliport cannot be named correctly by any
method on this page. This is the size of that population, and of everything
else.

```{r per-type}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(typ)) {
  for (rl in c("departures", "arrivals")) {
    x <- typ[typ$run == SHIPPED & typ$role == rl, ]
    if (nrow(x) == 0) next
    x <- x[order(-x$n_truth), ]
    cat(sprintf("\n**%s**\n\n", tools::toTitleCase(rl)))
    print(kable(data.frame(
      Class = x$apt_type, `Flights in truth` = num(x$n_truth),
      Aerodromes = num(x$n_aerodromes), Answered = num(x$n_answered),
      Correct = num(x$n_correct), Coverage = pct(x$coverage),
      Accuracy = pct(x$accuracy), check.names = FALSE),
      row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))
  }
  unn <- typ[typ$run == SHIPPED &
             !typ$apt_type %in% c("large_airport", "medium_airport"), ]
  if (nrow(unn)) {
    cat(sprintf("\nOutside the candidate set — %s classes, %s flights across both roles — the method is working against a reference it was never given. Those flights are counted in the denominator throughout this page, so every coverage figure here already carries their cost.\n",
                num(length(unique(unn$apt_type))), num(sum(unn$n_truth))))
  }
}
```

## Does any of it hold on a second period? {#sec-stability}

Everything above is one three-day sample. An argmax over hundreds of cells on a
single sample always flatters itself: part of the winning cell's margin is that
sample's noise, and noise does not reproduce. The only way to find out which
part is real is to measure a different period with the same code.

The second period is **5–7 June 2024**, chosen because the Network Manager
reference for that month is committed to the repository and the matching tracks
already exist from earlier versions of this study.

```{r stability}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (is.null(t24)) {
  cat("*The second-period sweep has not been staged yet.*\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("The 2024 sample carries %s ground-truth flights against 2025's %s.\n\n",
              num(t24$n_ground_truth[1]), num(N_GT)))

  s1_25 <- trend[trend$stage == 1, ]; s1_24 <- t24[t24$stage == 1, ]
  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("adep", "ades"), function(role) {
    b25 <- best_row(s1_25, role); b24 <- best_row(s1_24, role)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(list(
      list("trend ceiling", "fl_cap"), list("trend vote margin", "margin"),
      list("trend radius (NM)", "radius_nm")), function(pp_) {
        data.frame(Role = toupper(role), Parameter = pp_[[1]],
                   `2025 optimum` = b25[[pp_[[2]]]],
                   `2024 optimum` = b24[[pp_[[2]]]],
                   Agrees = ifelse(b25[[pp_[[2]]]] == b24[[pp_[[2]]]], "yes", "**no**"),
                   check.names = FALSE)
      }))
  }))
  print(kable(rows, row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))

  agree <- sum(rows$Agrees == "yes")
  cat(sprintf("\n%d of %d parameter optima agree across the two periods — which, taken alone, reads worse than the situation is. Comparing two argmaxes is close to the weakest test available: over hundreds of cells the top cell moves under noise even when the surface underneath is stable.\n",
              agree, nrow(rows)))

  # The question that matters is not whether the argmax moved but whether the
  # *decision* would have changed. Ranking every cell by both periods at once
  # answers that; comparing two argmaxes does not.
  key <- function(d) paste(d$fl_cap, d$margin, d$radius_nm, d$penalty_nm, sep = "/")
  a <- s1_25; b <- s1_24; a$key <- key(a); b$key <- key(b)
  mm <- merge(a, b, by = "key", suffixes = c("_25", "_24"))
  mm$joint <- mm$ades_score_25 / mm$n_ground_truth_25 +
              mm$ades_score_24 / mm$n_ground_truth_24
  o <- mm[order(-mm$joint), ]
  dtm <- datum_of(trend)
  nc <- nearest_cap(o$fl_cap_25, dtm)
  rk <- which(o$fl_cap_25 == nc$cap &
              o$margin_25 == SHIPPED_TREND$margin &
              o$radius_nm_25 == SHIPPED_TREND$radius_nm)

  if (!length(rk)) {
    cat("\n*(the shipped arrival cell is not present in both periods' grids, so its joint rank cannot be reported)*\n")
  } else {
    rk <- rk[1]
    cat(sprintf("\nSo the cells are ranked here by **both periods at once**, with each period's score divided by its own ground-truth count so the larger sample cannot dominate. On that ranking the shipped arrival configuration — %s, vote margin %g, %g NM, %g NM penalty — places **%d of %d**. The joint winner is %s / margin %g / %g NM, and differs by %s of normalised score.\n",
                cap_label(nc$cap, dtm), SHIPPED_TREND$margin,
                SHIPPED_TREND$radius_nm, SHIPPED_TREND$penalty_nm,
                rk, nrow(o),
                cap_label(o$fl_cap_25[1], dtm), o$margin_25[1], o$radius_nm_25[1],
                sprintf("%.5f", o$joint[1] - o$joint[rk])))
    if (!nc$exact) {
      cat(sprintf("\nOne substitution, stated rather than buried: the shipped ceiling is %s, and the research sweep's grid does not contain it — the grid was built around %s, the height equivalent of FL60. So %s stands in above, and the ranking is that cell's rank, not the shipped cell's. The pipeline grid in @sec-pipeline carries both values and is where the two are actually compared.\n",
                  cap_label(nc$want, dtm), cap_label(nc$cap, dtm),
                  cap_label(nc$cap, dtm)))
    }
    cat("\nThe arrival tuning therefore does hold on both periods. What moves between them is which of several near-equivalent cells happens to come first, and the radius is the parameter that moves.\n")
  }
}
```

```{r stability-endpoint}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
e24 <- cache("sweep_radius_height_2024.csv")
if (is.null(e24)) {
  cat("\n**The endpoint rule was not re-swept on the second period.** Its sweep runs over the cached candidate table, which exists for 2025 and not for 2024; building it for 2024 would mean either materialising an H3 index over the whole second period or reimplementing the pipeline's endpoint extraction in the harness. The second option is precisely the kind of shortcut @sec-pipeline exists to warn about, so neither was taken.\n")
  cat("\nThe departure recommendation therefore rests on a different guarantee, and a stronger one for this particular purpose: it was validated *in the pipeline itself* on 2025, where the sweep and `process_dai` agree to the flight. What is missing is a second sample, not a second implementation. It is listed in the limitations as the outstanding check.\n")
} else if (!is.null(grid)) {
  cat("\nFor the endpoint rule, which is what departures actually adopt:\n\n")
  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("adep", "ades"), function(role) {
    a <- best_row(grid, role); b <- best_row(e24, role)
    data.frame(Role = toupper(role),
               `2025 radius / height` = sprintf("%g NM / %s ft", a$radius_nm,
                    format(a$height_ft, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)),
               `2024 radius / height` = sprintf("%g NM / %s ft", b$radius_nm,
                    format(b$height_ft, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)),
               Agrees = ifelse(a$radius_nm == b$radius_nm & a$height_ft == b$height_ft,
                               "**yes**", "no"),
               check.names = FALSE)
  }))
  print(kable(rows, row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))
  cat(sprintf("\nThe departure optimum — the one that actually ships — is the *same cell* on two independent periods, out of %d. Neither period was consulted when the other was measured. That is the strongest stability evidence in this study.\n",
              nrow(e24)))
}
```

## What ships {#sec-defaults}

This table is **read from the runs themselves**, not written out here. The
`legacy` column is the configuration the `legacy` run was built with, and the
`ships` column is the configuration the `recommended` run was built with — and
`recommended` is constructed as a bare `DetectionConfig()`, so it is by
definition whatever the pipeline currently defaults to.

That matters more than it sounds. The equivalent table in version 6 was typed
by hand, and it had drifted: it named two values the code does not have. A
table asserting what ships, on a page whose whole argument is that hand-copied
figures cannot be trusted, is the one place that must not be hand-copied.

```{r what-ships}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (is.null(modes) || !"recommended" %in% modes$run) {
  cat("*(the pipeline runs have not been made against this checkout, so what ships cannot be read from them)*\n")
} else {
  L <- modes[modes$run == "legacy", ][1, ]
  S <- modes[modes$run == "recommended", ][1, ]

  fmtv <- function(v) {
    if (is.null(v) || length(v) == 0 || is.na(v)) return("—")
    if (is.numeric(v)) format(v, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)
    else as.character(v)
  }

  # Ordering is deliberate: the ranking rule first, because without it none of
  # the rest holds; the datum second, because it decides what the ceiling
  # underneath it even means.
  spec <- list(
    list("trend_rank_by", "The enabling change. Ring-count selection discarded candidates before measuring them; every tuned trend value fails under it and gains under exact distance."),
    list("trend_max_datum", "@sec-datum. Aligns `trend`'s altitude cut with every other altitude gate in the pipeline."),
    list("trend_max_height_ft", "The ceiling that datum is measured against, and inert while the datum is `msl` — which is why the legacy column shows a value legacy never applied. See @sec-pipeline on 6,000 against 6,100."),
    list("trend_max_fl", "Retained, and inert while the datum is `field`. It is what `legacy()` reads, so published lists stay reproducible."),
    list("trend_radius_nm", "Swept in @sec-trend-sweep and through the pipeline in @sec-pipeline."),
    list("trend_vote_margin", "Sweep harness only — the pipeline grid holds it fixed. The weakest-supported value here."),
    list("trend_sched_penalty_nm", "A tie-break `trend` never had. The single largest contributor to the arrival gain."),
    list("endpoint_radius_nm", "Interior optimum; the pipeline reproduces the sweep exactly."),
    list("endpoint_height_ft", "A height above field elevation, and always was."),
    list("endpoint_sched_penalty_nm", "Unchanged.")
  )

  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(spec, function(s) {
    p <- s[[1]]
    if (!p %in% names(modes)) return(NULL)
    lv <- fmtv(L[[p]]); sv <- fmtv(S[[p]])
    data.frame(Parameter = sprintf("`%s`", p),
               Legacy = lv,
               Ships = if (identical(lv, sv)) sv else sprintf("**%s**", sv),
               Evidence = s[[2]], check.names = FALSE)
  }))
  print(kable(rows, row.names = FALSE))
  changed <- sum(rows$Legacy != gsub("\\*\\*", "", rows$Ships))
  cat(sprintf("\n%d of the %d parameters differ from the legacy constants.\n",
              changed, nrow(rows)))
}
```

```{r ships-vs-study}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# Does what ships match what this study recommends?
#
# `recommended` is a bare DetectionConfig(); `combined` is assembled from the
# sweep optima. Where they differ, the pipeline is running something the study
# did not choose -- which is worth surfacing rather than leaving for a reader
# to notice by comparing two tables.
if (!is.null(modes) && all(c("recommended", "combined") %in% modes$run)) {
  R <- modes[modes$run == "recommended", ][1, ]
  C <- modes[modes$run == "combined", ][1, ]
  pars <- intersect(c("trend_radius_nm", "trend_vote_margin", "trend_ceiling",
                      "trend_sched_penalty_nm", "trend_rank_by"), names(modes))
  diff <- pars[sapply(pars, function(p) !isTRUE(all.equal(R[[p]], C[[p]])))]
  if (length(diff)) {
    cat("::: {.callout-important}\n## What ships is not what the sweeps chose\n\n")
    cat("The shipped configuration and this study's swept optimum differ in",
        length(diff), "parameter(s):\n\n")
    cat("| Parameter | Ships | Sweep optimum |\n|---|---|---|\n")
    for (p in diff)
      cat(sprintf("| `%s` | %s | %s |\n", p,
                  format(R[[p]], trim = TRUE), format(C[[p]], trim = TRUE)))
    cat(sprintf("\nBoth are measured above: `recommended` is the shipped row, `combined` the swept one, and on arrivals they score %s against %s. This is reported rather than resolved — changing a published default is a decision for the pipeline's maintainers, and this page's job is to make the gap visible.\n:::\n",
                num(R$ades_score), num(C$ades_score)))
  }
}
```

```{r ceiling-6000-6100}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
tgc <- cache("trend_grid_v6.csv")
if (is.null(tgc)) {
  cat("*(the pipeline ceiling grid has not been run against this checkout, so the 6,000 against 6,100 question is not settled here)*\n")
} else {
  capof <- function(run) as.numeric(sub("^grid_h([0-9]+)_.*$", "\\1", run))
  g <- tgc[grepl("^grid_h", tgc$run), ]
  g$cap <- capof(g$run)
  best <- function(cap) {
    x <- g[g$cap == cap, ]
    if (!nrow(x)) return(NA_real_) else max(x$ades_score)
  }
  s6000 <- best(6000)
  s6100 <- best(6100)
  if (!is.na(s6000) && !is.na(s6100)) {
    d <- s6100 - s6000
    cat(sprintf("**6,000 ft or 6,100?** The shipped ceiling is 6,000 ft; the research sweep called 6,100 optimal — on a grid that never contained 6,000, so that recommendation was never a comparison. Run through `process_dai` itself, the best arrival score at 6,000 ft is %s and at 6,100 ft is %s, a difference of %s. %s\n\n",
      num(s6000), num(s6100), sgn(d),
      if (abs(d) < 50)
        "That is inside what one three-day sample resolves, so the shipped 6,000 ft stands: there is no measured reason to move it, and moving a published constant needs one."
      else if (d > 0)
        "The pipeline prefers 6,100 ft, and by more than sampling noise. That is a recommendation to move the shipped ceiling, and it is recorded here rather than acted on inside this study."
      else
        "The pipeline prefers the shipped 6,000 ft, so the sweep's preference for 6,100 does not survive contact with production — the same pattern version 6 found for its flight-level cap."))
  }
}
```

The ceiling and the vote margin were **rejected earlier in this study and
reinstated**. That rejection was measured under ring-count selection, where
raising the ceiling genuinely did lose ground. The lesson is not that the first
measurement was careless but that it answered a narrower question than it
appeared to: *given this selection rule*, the tuning fails. Changing the rule
changed the answer.

The radius is a different story, and version 6 told it wrongly. Its table
recorded `trend_radius_nm` as shipping at 20 NM. The table above — read from a
bare `DetectionConfig()` rather than typed — shows it at **30 NM**, unchanged
from legacy. The recommendation was made and never applied, and no later
version noticed because every later version copied the claim rather than
measuring it.

Every OPDI flight list published before this change was built with the
legacy column, and `DetectionConfig.legacy()` still returns exactly those
values — including `trend_rank_by = "ring"` — so anything already released
stays reproducible by name. That is the same principle as the frozen `version`
strings on published events. A regression test pins the preset, a second pins
the shipped values, and a third asserts the two differ, so the preset cannot
quietly become vacuous.

::: {.callout-warning}
### Is what ships what the pipeline prefers? {#sec-parity}

The question every earlier version answered by assertion. It is answerable
now, and only now, because the grid was widened until it contained the shipped
configuration: it previously fixed the vote margin at 2 while `DetectionConfig`
ships 0, so main's own cell had never been run.

```{r parity}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
tgp <- cache("trend_grid_v6.csv")
if (is.null(tgp)) {
  cat("*(the pipeline grid has not been run against this checkout)*\n")
} else {
  g <- tgp[grepl("^grid_h", tgp$run), ]
  g <- g[order(-g$ades_score), ]
  # The shipped configuration, named once in the setup chunk.
  hit <- which(g$trend_ceiling == SHIPPED_TREND$ceiling_field &
               g$trend_radius_nm == SHIPPED_TREND$radius_nm &
               g$trend_vote_margin == SHIPPED_TREND$margin)
  if (!length(hit)) {
    cat("::: {.callout-important}\n## Not checkable\n\nThe shipped configuration is not among the grid's cells, so this cannot be answered. Widen the grid.\n:::\n")
  } else {
    r <- hit[1]
    gap <- g$ades_score[1] - g$ades_score[r]
    cat(sprintf("The shipped configuration — %s, %g NM, vote margin %g — places **%d of %d** cells, %s behind the best.\n\n",
                cap_label(SHIPPED_TREND$ceiling_field, "field"),
                SHIPPED_TREND$radius_nm, SHIPPED_TREND$margin,
                r, nrow(g), if (gap == 0) "level" else sgn(-gap)))
    if (r == 1) {
      cat("It **is** the best cell. Every parameter version 6 recommended and\nwhich was never applied — a 6,100 ft ceiling, a vote margin of 2, a 20 NM\nradius — loses to the value that actually ships:\n\n")
      cmp <- function(col, alt, label) {
        keep <- g[g$trend_ceiling == SHIPPED_TREND$ceiling_field &
                  g$trend_radius_nm == SHIPPED_TREND$radius_nm &
                  g$trend_vote_margin == SHIPPED_TREND$margin, ]
        oth <- g[g[[col]] == alt, ]
        for (nm in setdiff(c("trend_ceiling", "trend_radius_nm", "trend_vote_margin"), col))
          oth <- oth[oth[[nm]] == keep[[nm]][1], ]
        if (!nrow(oth) || !nrow(keep)) return(NULL)
        data.frame(Parameter = label,
                   `Version 6 recommended` = alt,
                   `Ships` = keep[[col]][1],
                   `Cost of v6's value` = sgn(oth$ades_score[1] - keep$ades_score[1]),
                   check.names = FALSE)
      }
      rows <- do.call(rbind, list(
        cmp("trend_ceiling", 6100, "altitude ceiling (ft above field)"),
        cmp("trend_vote_margin", 2, "vote margin"),
        cmp("trend_radius_nm", 20, "detection radius (NM)")))
      if (!is.null(rows)) print(kable(rows, row.names = FALSE))
      cat("\nSo the recommendations were not merely un-applied; applying them would\nhave made arrival detection worse. `benchmarks/check_main_parity.py`\nasserts this on every run, and fails if the two ever part company.\n")
    } else {
      cat("It is **not** the best cell. That is reported, not resolved: changing a published default is the pipeline maintainers' decision, and this study's job is to make the gap visible.\n")
    }
  }
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this check cannot see

The grid varies three parameters at one penalty and one ranking rule, on one
three-day period, with `process_dai` unable to read the 2024 tracks. And the
pipeline is not bit-reproducible: re-running moves a handful of flights where
two aerodromes tie on effective distance, worth about ±15 points of score. A
difference smaller than that is not a difference.

The ceiling comparison below sits at roughly two to three times that bound and
is consistent in sign across all six radius-and-margin combinations, which is
why it is reported as a result rather than as noise.
:::


## Running it {#sec-running}

The configuration this report recommends is the **default**. `adep_mode` and
`ades_mode` default to `None`, which means the pipeline uses `DetectionConfig`'s
own values — so you get the recommendation by not overriding anything.

Step `03` is the flight list: one row per track, carrying ADEP and ADES.

```python
from datetime import date
from opdi.runner import run_pipeline

run_pipeline(
    env="opensky",              # plain parquet over S3A; no Hive, no Iceberg
    step="03",
    start_date=date(2025, 6, 1),
    end_date=date(2025, 6, 30),
)
```

The same thing from a shell, using the installed console script:

```bash
opdi run --env opensky --step 03 --start 2025-06-01 --end 2025-06-30
```

To depart from the recommendation, name the methods explicitly. Both accept
`trend`, `endpoint` or `nearest`:

```bash
opdi run --env opensky --step 03 --start 2025-06-01 --end 2025-06-30 \
         --adep-mode trend --ades-mode trend
```

That example asks for `trend` on both roles — the pre-2026 behaviour, and the
`legacy` row in every comparison on this page.

**Step 03 does not stand alone.** It reads the tracks written by step `02` and
the aerodrome zones from step `00`, so those must have run for the same period
first. Omitting `--step` runs the whole chain in order.

::: {.callout-note}
## What "recommended" means here, and how it is kept honest

The values are not written into this page. @sec-defaults reads them from a
bare `DetectionConfig()` — the same object the pipeline constructs — so the
table cannot describe a configuration the code does not have. The equivalent
table in version 6 was typed by hand and named two values the code never had,
for three versions.

`benchmarks/check_main_parity.py` closes the loop the other way: it compares
that configuration against the best cell of the pipeline grid, which is the
only sweep that runs the shipped package rather than a re-implementation of
it.
:::

## Re-running a past month will not reproduce it
These defaults change ADEP and ADES for any month re-processed with them. That
is intended, and it is why the old behaviour remains reachable by name rather
than being deleted. A new algorithm gets a new `version`; the published one is
never mutated.
:::

## Provenance {#sec-provenance}

Each row is one file this page reads: the job that produced it, the commit it
was produced at, and when. Every figure on this page is regenerated by
`benchmarks/regenerate_v62.py`, which the page runs before drawing anything, so
a row marked **unverified** would mean a file staged outside that chain and
traceable to no command.

```{r provenance}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
mf <- file.path("data", "_manifest.json")
if (!requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cat("*jsonlite not available; provenance table skipped.*\n")
} else if (!file.exists(mf)) {
  cat("**No manifest.** Every CSV here was staged by hand and none can be traced to the command that produced it.\n")
} else {
  m <- jsonlite::fromJSON(mf, simplifyDataFrame = FALSE)
  files <- sort(list.files("data", pattern = "[.]csv$"))
  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files, function(f) {
    e <- m[[f]]
    if (is.null(e)) {
      data.frame(File = f, Job = "**unverified**", Commit = "—",
                 Produced = "—", check.names = FALSE)
    } else {
      data.frame(File = f, Job = basename(e$script),
                 Commit = paste0(e$git_sha, if (isTRUE(e$git_dirty)) " (dirty)" else ""),
                 Produced = substr(e$produced_utc, 1, 16), check.names = FALSE)
    }
  }))
  print(kable(rows, row.names = FALSE, align = "l"))
  n_un <- sum(rows$Job == "**unverified**")
  cat(sprintf("\n%d files, %d traced to a command, %d unverified.\n",
              nrow(rows), nrow(rows) - n_un, n_un))
}
```

### Where reproducibility stops

Two boundaries, stated rather than implied.

**Ground truth cannot be rebuilt here.** `research/reference` is extracted by
the `eurocontrol` R package against the PRISME Oracle warehouse, which no run
on this cluster can reach. It is an external input, and every figure on this
page is measured against it.

**The upstream tables are rebuilt only when absent.** Reference zones, state
vectors and tracks are produced by declared stages, but a stage whose table is
already present records its identity rather than rebuilding it — because
regenerating the airport zone table would change the candidate set under the
whole study. For this version they *were* rebuilt, from the archive upward,
because the sampler changed.

### What moved underneath this version {#sec-drift}

This version sets out to recompute version 6's study with **one** variable
changed. That is a checkable claim, and it does not fully hold. Stating where
it fails is the point of recording input identities in the first place.

```{r input-drift}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
dr <- read_if("input_drift.csv")
if (is.null(dr)) {
  cat("*(the drift check has not been run against this checkout)*\n")
} else {
  show <- data.frame(
    Table   = dr$table,
    Objects = sprintf("%s → %s", dr$baseline_objects, dr$now_objects),
    Size    = sprintf("%.2f → %.2f GB", dr$baseline_bytes / 1e9, dr$now_bytes / 1e9),
    `Newest` = sprintf("%s → %s", substr(dr$baseline_newest, 1, 10),
                       ifelse(dr$now_newest == "", "—", substr(dr$now_newest, 1, 10))),
    Verdict = dr$verdict,
    check.names = FALSE)
  print(kable(show, row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))

  reb <- dr$table[dr$verdict == "REBUILT"]
  mk  <- dr$table[dr$verdict == "marker only"]
  if (length(mk)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n**%s**: byte-identical, same timestamp, one object fewer. That is the zero-byte directory marker MinIO leaves behind, which `provenance.s3_identity` stopped counting after it made a *deleted* table look populated. Bookkeeping, with no consequence for any figure.\n",
                paste(sprintf("`%s`", mk), collapse = ", ")))
  }
  if (length(reb)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n**%s**: genuinely rebuilt since version 6 recorded them. Every figure derived from them moved, and the datum does not explain any of it.\n",
                paste(sprintf("`%s`", reb), collapse = ", ")))
  }
}
```

The one that matters is **`opdi_endpoint_candidates`**, rebuilt after version 6
published: `r if (!is.null(dr)) { x <- dr[dr$table == "opdi_endpoint_candidates", ]; if (nrow(x)) sprintf("about %.0f%% smaller", 100 * (x$baseline_bytes - x$now_bytes) / x$baseline_bytes) else "smaller" } else "smaller"`, with the fresh-broadcast share roughly tripled —
the signature of stale-broadcast removal, which the PRC challenge results
recommend and which `endpoint` reads directly.

Two consequences, and they pull in opposite directions.

**The ground truth did *not* move.** `research/reference` grew by more than
half, but it grew by gaining *other periods*: this study's three-day slice is
unchanged, at `r num(as.numeric(trend$n_ground_truth[1]))` reference flights on
2025 and `r if (!is.null(t24)) num(as.numeric(t24$n_ground_truth[1])) else "—"`
on 2024 — the same counts version 6 reported. That is confirmed independently by @sec-equivalence,
where the sea-level sweep reproduces version 6's cell for cell. So every
denominator on this page is the one version 6 used, and the internal
comparisons — which are what this study actually argues from — are sound.

**But the endpoint-family numbers are not comparable to version 6's.** The
endpoint sweeps, the bearing test and the vertical measures all read the
rebuilt candidate table. Their figures differ from version 6's, and that
difference is a data change rather than a finding.

::: {.callout-warning}
## A verification this version cannot make

The intention was to verify directly that the datum change leaves departures
alone: the endpoint family is datum-independent by construction, so recomputing
it under the new code and recovering version 6's numbers would have settled it.

The candidate rebuild makes that comparison uncontrolled, so the verification is
**not available** and is not claimed. What remains is the within-study evidence
in @sec-bands — departures gain nothing in *any* elevation band, measured
where both arms read the same candidate table. That is genuine evidence and it
is weaker than the check that was intended.
:::

## Limitations {#sec-limitations}

### Parameters that were not swept

Five parameters were held fixed by decision rather than by evidence. Naming
them matters: a reader who sees seven tuned values and no caveat will
reasonably assume the whole configuration was optimised, and it was not.

| Parameter | Where | Held at | Why not swept |
|---|---|---|---|
| Smoothing half-window | `flights.py` | 2 samples | Parameterised in config so it is visible and changeable, but a smoothing width interacts with the sample rate rather than the geometry, and the decimation study settled the sample rate separately. |
| Classification dead band | `flights.py` | none exists | There is no dead band to sweep. The vote margin already plays that role. |
| Out-of-area border margin | `flights.py` | 30 NM | Fixes what counts as "outside the observed area". Changing it redefines the ground truth rather than the method, so a sweep would move the target as well as the aim. |
| Aerodrome type set | `h3_airport_zones.py` | large + medium | The candidate set. Widening it is a data-volume decision about the zone table, not a detection threshold. |
| H3 resolution | `config.py` | 7 (±0.76 NM) | Changing it invalidates every cached zone table. It no longer decides which candidates survive — that is exact distance now — but it still decides which aerodromes become candidates at all. |

Two of these carry a cost that this study measures rather than waves at, since
"not swept" is not the same as "no consequence".

```{r unswept-cost}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(typ) && !is.null(modes)) {
  out <- typ[typ$run == SHIPPED &
             !typ$apt_type %in% c("large_airport", "medium_airport", "out of area"), ]
  ooa <- typ[typ$run == SHIPPED & typ$apt_type == "out of area", ]
  m <- function(run, f) modes[[f]][modes$run == run][1]

  # Aggregated over roles: the frame carries one row per (class, role), and
  # listing them separately reads as four classes rather than two.
  byclass <- tapply(out$n_truth, out$apt_type, sum)
  cat(sprintf("**The type set.** %s flights across both roles have a true aerodrome outside the large/medium candidate set (%s). No method on this page can name them, whatever its thresholds, because the aerodrome is not among the candidates. They are counted in every denominator here, so each coverage figure already carries their cost: they are worth about %s of headline coverage.\n\n",
              num(sum(out$n_truth)),
              paste(sprintf("%s at %ss", num(byclass), gsub("_", " ", names(byclass))),
                    collapse = ", "),
              pct(sum(out$n_truth) / (2 * N_GT))))

  cat(sprintf("**The border margin.** Fixed at 30 NM, it decides which flights are labelled out-of-area. %s of ground-truth departures genuinely begin outside the observed area, and the recommended configuration recognises %s of them — at %s precision, so the label is trustworthy when it appears but is rarely reached. For arrivals the recall is %s: `trend` emits no out-of-area label at all, which is a structural property of the vote rule rather than a tuning choice.\n\n",
              pct(m("recommended", "adep_gt_ooa_share")),
              pct(m("recommended", "adep_ooa_recall")),
              pct(m("recommended", "adep_ooa_precision")),
              pct(m("recommended", "ades_ooa_recall"))))

  cat(sprintf("Both costs fall on coverage rather than accuracy, which is the benign direction: with the free out-of-area wins removed, in-area accuracy is %s for departures and %s for arrivals.\n",
              pct(m("recommended", "adep_inarea_accuracy")),
              pct(m("recommended", "ades_inarea_accuracy"))))
}
```

### `trend` cannot say "out of area"

`trend` names an aerodrome or says nothing. It has no way to report that a
flight began or ended outside the observed area, because the vote rule only
ever considers aerodromes the aircraft flew near — silence and *outside* are
the same output.

That is not a small omission for the shipped configuration, which takes
arrivals from `trend`:

```{r ooa-gap}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(modes)) {
  m <- function(run, f) modes[[f]][modes$run == run][1]
  cat(sprintf("%s of reference arrivals genuinely come from outside the observed area, and **none of them can be labelled as such**. Departures ship `endpoint`, which does emit the label: %s precision, so it is trustworthy when it appears, but only %s recall.\n",
              pct(m(SHIPPED, "ades_gt_ooa_share")),
              pct(m(SHIPPED, "adep_ooa_precision")),
              pct(m(SHIPPED, "adep_ooa_recall"))))
}
```

`endpoint` already has the mechanism — a fix at the edge of the ingestion
region rather than near any aerodrome — so giving `trend` the same test is a
port, not an invention. It is the clearest single improvement left on this page
and is not implemented here.

### The grid stops before the departure optimum does

The pipeline grid runs to 10,000 ft above field, and departures under `trend`
are still rising there. The research sweep goes further and does turn —
departures peak near the top of its range on both periods, then fall away as
accuracy drops faster than coverage rises — but "it turns in the sweep" is
weaker evidence than "it turns in the pipeline", and the two have disagreed
before.

This costs nothing that ships, because departures are served by `endpoint` and
the arrival optimum is comfortably interior on both periods and in both stages.
It does mean the departure half of the trend grid should not be quoted as an
optimum.

### One sample, and what that does and does not license

The parameters are chosen as the argmax over a grid evaluated on a single
three-day period. An argmax over hundreds of cells on one sample will always
overstate the gain slightly: some of the winning cell's margin is the sample's
noise, and it will not reproduce.

That is the reason for the second period, and for reporting the shape of each
optimum rather than only its location. A parameter sitting on a broad plateau
is a safe recommendation even from one sample; one sitting on a sharp isolated
peak is not, however good its score.

### The second period confirms through the sweeps, not the pipeline

Every pipeline number on this page is 2025-06-05…07. The 2024 tracks pre-date
this study's H3 indexing and `process_dai` reads `h3_res_7` off the track table
directly, so the pipeline arms cannot run on that period at all — version 6 met
the same wall and ran the pipeline on 2025 alone. @sec-ceiling states the
consequence where it arises.

Repeated here because it bounds every two-period claim in this report: the
second period tests the ceiling and the datum comparison, which is the part
most at risk of being a one-sample artefact, and it does **not** independently
reproduce the band breakdown, the tuning ladder, or the pipeline fidelity
check. A caveat that appears only beside the result it qualifies is easy to
read past.

### The `>3000` band needs a different question

The highest elevation band is not a datum problem and this study cannot fix it.
Recall there is under one percent on **both** datums, which is a coverage
failure upstream of detection: the aerodrome never becomes a candidate, so no
threshold anywhere in `trend` can reach it. Whether that is receiver geometry
over the Anatolian plateau or something in ingestion is worth knowing and is
not this study's question.

It is worth stating plainly because that band is where an elevation-aware cut
should have helped most, and the fact that it did not is evidence about
coverage rather than evidence against the datum — @sec-bands.

## Appendix A — The busiest 100 aerodromes {#sec-top100}

Movement counts are what OPDI is for, so the last check is per aerodrome rather
than per flight: for each of the hundred busiest in the reference, how many
movements the recommended methodology finds, against how many the Network
Manager data says there were, and how the legacy algorithm
compares on the same aerodromes.

The matching is **flight by flight, not count against count**. Each reference
flight is paired with an OPDI track on aircraft address (`icao24`) plus
callsign plus date, and where several tracks match, the one starting closest to
the reference off-block time. The columns then mean:

| Column | Definition |
|---|---|
| Movements (truth) | Reference flights whose true aerodrome is this one. |
| Found | Of those, how many OPDI gave any answer for. |
| Correct | Of those, how many OPDI attributed to **this** aerodrome. |
| Count ratio | Movements OPDI *assigns to* this aerodrome ÷ movements in truth. Includes flights that truly belong elsewhere, so it is what an operational count would show, and it can exceed 1. |
| Recall | Correct ÷ movements in truth. **Per-aerodrome recall** — not the out-of-area recall of @sec-metrics, which is a different measure sharing the word. |
| Recall, legacy | The same, for the algorithm published before 2026. |

```{r top100}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(apt)) {
  for (rl in c("departures", "arrivals")) {
    r <- apt[apt$run == SHIPPED & apt$role == rl & apt$airport != "OOA", ]
    l <- apt[apt$run == "legacy"      & apt$role == rl & apt$airport != "OOA", ]
    if (nrow(r) == 0) next
    r <- r[order(-r$n_truth), ][1:min(100, nrow(r)), ]
    l <- l[match(r$airport, l$airport), ]
    cat(sprintf("\n### %s\n\n", tools::toTitleCase(rl)))
    print(kable(data.frame(
      `#` = seq_len(nrow(r)),
      Aerodrome = r$airport,
      `Movements (truth)` = num(r$n_truth),
      `Found` = num(r$n_predicted_here),
      `Correct` = num(r$n_correct),
      `Count ratio` = sprintf("%.3f", r$count_ratio),
      `Recall` = pct(r$recall),
      `Recall, legacy` = pct(l$recall),
      `Δ recall` = pp(r$recall - l$recall),
      check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))
  }
}
```

```{r top100-summary}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(apt)) {
  cat("\n### Across the hundred\n\n")
  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("departures", "arrivals"), function(rl) {
    r <- apt[apt$run == SHIPPED & apt$role == rl & apt$airport != "OOA", ]
    l <- apt[apt$run == "legacy"      & apt$role == rl & apt$airport != "OOA", ]
    r <- r[order(-r$n_truth), ][1:min(100, nrow(r)), ]
    l <- l[match(r$airport, l$airport), ]
    data.frame(
      Role = tools::toTitleCase(rl),
      `Movements in truth` = num(sum(r$n_truth)),
      `Recall, shipped` = pct(sum(r$n_correct) / sum(r$n_truth)),
      `Recall, legacy`  = pct(sum(l$n_correct, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(l$n_truth, na.rm = TRUE)),
      `Aerodromes improved` = sprintf("%d of %d", sum(r$recall > l$recall, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(r)),
      `Median count ratio`  = sprintf("%.3f", median(r$count_ratio, na.rm = TRUE)),
      check.names = FALSE)
  }))
  print(kable(rows, row.names = FALSE, align = "r"))
  cat("\nA count ratio below one means the aerodrome is under-counted — the usual case, since every abstention is a movement not attributed. Above one means movements are being attributed to an aerodrome that did not see them, which is the more damaging error and the one the scoring penalises at rate $k$.\n")
  cat("\nThe departure row is the result: recall rises by nearly nine points and the median aerodrome is within about one percent of its true movement count.\n")
  arr <- rows[rows$Role == "Arrivals", ]
  cat(sprintf("\n**The arrival row must be read with @sec-verdict in hand.** Recall reads %s against legacy's %s, improving on %s — which looks like a mild regression and is not one. Measured as an algorithm on a trend-only flight list, arrivals gain; the shortfall here comes from the merged list also containing departure-only tracks, which this table pairs with reference flights by start time, so some arrivals are counted against a track that carries none. The measurement moved; the data did not. It is left in the table rather than corrected away, because a benchmark that quietly adjusts its own alignment to flatter a result is worth less than one that shows where it is fragile.\n",
              arr$`Recall, shipped`, arr$`Recall, legacy`,
              arr$`Aerodromes improved`))
}
```
